findings.issue: contradicts task clause 'printing which bugs and held phases it is releasing over when a bypass is armed' on the surface the owner reads: no_open_bugs is called through run(), which in the default (non-LOUD, non-CI) mode sends the step's output to $WORKDIR/step.log and prints only 'ok' when the step passes. The 'ok: released over by #release-with-bugs armed for this session: ...' sentence that release.py permitted prints is therefore discarded in exactly the armed-green case. The same holds under release.py's verify-release step, which keeps only 'tools/verify.sh --release is green' (release.py:428-431). rl20b asserts the function's own stdout contains BUG-4, not that the verify row shows it, so the executor's claim 'names what it releases over' is true of the function and untrue of a local verify.sh --release run.
findings.resolution: Make the armed-green case reach the terminal: have no_open_bugs print the verdict line to stderr or to a channel run() does not capture, or have run() show the log of a step that opts in. Add a rl20 case that runs the verify.sh row quietly and asserts the 'released over' line appears in what the user sees.

findings.issue: The test that an unreadable plan still refuses has no case on the new path. The refusal branch ('could not read the release status', release.py:182) is reached by no rl case: rl17-rl20b all use a readable plan, and a grep of release.py finds no case that reads a missing or garbled plan. Deleting the `if bug_problem or phase_problem` branch would turn an unreadable plan into 'the plan carries no open bug and no held phase' (bugs and held both empty, so it returns True), and no case would go red. The executor's mutation list (bypass, session, always-refuse, held dropped, exit code, old reader) did not include it. By reading, the code refuses today; nothing keeps it so, in a release guard.
findings.resolution: Add a case with a plan that does not parse, and a missing plan, asserting `permitted --repo` exits 1 and the line starts 'refused: could not read'. Run that case with and without an armed slot, so the armed + unreadable direction is pinned too.

findings.issue: 'One predicate' holds for the readers (read_bugs, read_held_phases, bypass_armed, refusal, KEYWORD are all the guard's) but not for the decision. release_verdict restates the control flow of guard-release.py decide() (nothing held -> pass, armed -> pass, else refuse) and the two already differ: decide() lets an armed slot release over an unreadable list (`if not (bugs or bug_problem or held or phase_problem): continue; if bypass_armed: return None`), and arm-release-bypass.py's docstring tells the owner 'the armed slot releases over that refusal too'. release_verdict refuses it even when armed. The refusal is the safer direction and matches the review requirement, but the owner is told one thing at arming time and verify.sh does another. The executor named this as a known leftover; it is the one place verify.sh, release.py and the hook do not answer alike.
findings.resolution: Move the decision into guard-release.py as one function (e.g. a verdict(project, session_id) returning allowed + sentence) that decide() and release_verdict both call, and settle the armed-over-unreadable question once. If refusing is intended, change the arming message and decide() to match; if release is intended, pin it with a case. Either way one place states it.

preExisting.issue: bypass_armed with a missing session id reads release-bypass-none.json, the same name arm-release-bypass.py writes when it is handed no session id, so a slot armed with no session id is honoured by any caller that also has none. Not changed by this diff and release.py permitted inherits it as the guard does.
preExisting.resolution: Treat an empty or missing session id as 'no slot can be looked up' in bypass_armed and in arm().

intent.note: Does what was asked on the main clauses: verify.sh's no_open_bugs is now `python3 tools/release.py permitted`, a small CLI over release_verdict, which is built only from the guard hook's read_bugs / read_held_phases / bypass_armed / refusal / KEYWORD; release_permitted is a thin wrapper over it, so the pipeline's remote steps and the verify step share one reader. An open bug or held phase with no slot is exit 1 naming it; a live slot for this session is exit 0 naming what it releases over; an expired slot, another session's slot or no session id is exit 1; the held-phase half is covered the same way (rl17..rl20b). Nothing in the diff writes a slot except inside scratch fixtures; the only writer remains the UserPromptSubmit hook, so nothing the model writes arms it. An unreadable plan refuses (release.py:181-183), armed or not. Divergence, quoting the clause 'printing which bugs and held phases it is releasing over when a bypass is armed' against verify.sh run() (lines 237-264): in the default mode the step's output goes to a log shown only on failure, so the armed-green line is never shown. The executor's claim 'names what it releases over' therefore describes the function and not a local verify.sh --release. Also the filed tests are in release.py's own selftest because tests/test_verify_sh.py does not exist, which the outcome says plainly. The dependants named (ci.yml, affected.py, check-example-pins.py, _refs.py, test__refs.py, guard-release.py's publisher reader) are answered and nothing in the diff contradicts the answers.
